- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) are common; cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high or 1.2x prior peak.
- Model often lags in early horizon (1-3 days) — if sentiment is trending, forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.0% per day for momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show price decline, model tends to hold or overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until trend stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mid-term (days 10–20) when sentiment is mixed; cap forecast at 1.1x recent 14-day average to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to “stick” to prior trend; shift forecast toward sentiment-weighted average of last 7 days.
